units.text: The First Pillar of Islam: Its Meaning and Implications

First question: Please explain to us the meaning of the first pillar of Islam and what that meaning entails. How is it realized by a person? And what is the ruling on someone who is ignorant of any part of it?

Answer: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Praise be to Allah, and may blessings and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah, his family, his companions, and those who follow his guidance. To proceed:

Allah sent His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to all people: Arabs and non-Arabs, jinn and humans, males and females, calling them to the oneness of Allah and sincerity to Him, to believe in him (peace and blessings be upon him) and in what he brought, to believe in all the messengers, all the angels, the books sent down from heaven, the Last Day—which is the resurrection, the gathering, the recompense, the reckoning, Paradise, and Hell—and to believe in the Divine Decree, its good and its evil. Allah decreed all things, knew them, enumerated them, and wrote them (glorified and exalted be He). Everything that occurs happens by Allah's decree, predestination, and effective will (glorified and exalted be He). He commanded people to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. This is the first thing to which the Prophet ﷺ called, and it is the first pillar of Islam: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. When he said to the people, "Say: there is no god but Allah," and commanded them to believe that he is the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), most of them refused and rejected this call. The Quraysh said to him what Allah mentioned about them: ⟦Q1⟧ [p.5].

And He (glorified be He) said about them: ⟦Q2⟧ [al-Saffat:35-36]. They found this call strange because they had lived upon the worship of idols, images, and these deities besides Allah (mighty and majestic be He). Therefore, they rejected the Messenger's call to the oneness of Allah and sincerity to Him. What he called to, peace be upon him, is what all the messengers called to, as He (glorified and exalted be He) said: ⟦Q3⟧ [al-Nahl:36]. And He (glorified be He) said: ⟦Q4⟧ [al-Anbiya:25].

In the two Sahihs, from Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing prayer, giving zakah (obligatory almsgiving), fasting Ramadan, and pilgrimage to the House."

Also in the Sahih, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), that a questioner came to the Prophet ﷺ in the form of a man with very white clothes and very black hair, no trace of travel upon him, and none of those present knew him. He said, "O Muhammad, tell me about Islam." He said: "Islam is to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to establish prayer, to give zakah, to fast Ramadan, and to perform pilgrimage to the House if you are able to find a way." He said, "You have spoken the truth." The companions said, "We were amazed that he asked him and then confirmed him." Then he said, "Tell me about iman (faith)." He said: "Iman is to believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and to believe in the Divine Decree, its good and its evil." He said, "You have spoken the truth." He said, "Tell me about ihsan (excellence)." He said: "To worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you." The rest of the hadith.

Then the Prophet ﷺ informed them that this questioner was Gabriel (peace be upon him), who came to teach them their religion. Since they had not asked, Gabriel came by Allah's command to ask about this great religion so they would learn and benefit. The religion of Islam is built upon these five outward pillars:
First: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.
Second: establishing the five prayers.
Third: paying zakah.

Fourth: fasting Ramadan.
Fifth: pilgrimage to the Sacred House of Allah for those able to find a way.
And upon inward pillars of faith in the heart, which are: belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the Divine Decree, its good and its evil.
It is necessary to have these fundamentals, that the accountable person believes in these six inward fundamentals connected to the heart: to believe that Allah is his Lord and God, and He is the Truth (glorified and exalted be He); to believe in Allah's angels, in Allah's books that He sent down to the prophets, such as the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, the Qur'an, and other books sent to the prophets; to also believe in the messengers whom Allah sent to His servants, the first of them being Noah and the last of them Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him). They are many, and Allah has mentioned some of them in the Glorious Qur'an. To also believe in the Last Day, which is the resurrection after death, the reckoning, the recompense, and all the affairs of the Hereafter. The people of faith will have happiness and Paradise, and the people of disbelief will have loss, regret, and the Fire. It is also necessary to believe in the Divine Decree, its good and its evil, and that Allah decreed all things, knew them, wrote them, and enumerated them. Whatever Allah wills happens, and whatever He does not will does not happen. Everything in existence—good, evil, obedience, disobedience—has been preceded by Allah's knowledge, book, and decree (glorified and exalted be He).
The first great fundamental with which the messengers came is: belief that Allah is the true God (glorified and exalted be He). This is the meaning of the testimony that there is no god but Allah. This is the essential root upon which all the messengers (peace and blessings be upon them) agreed; they all called to this essential root: that people believe that Allah is the true God and that none has the right to be worshipped but Him. This is the meaning of "la ilaha illa Allah"—there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah. Whatever people worship—idols, trees, stones, prophets, saints, or angels—is all false. True worship is for Allah alone (glorified and exalted be He), as He said (glorified be He): ⟦Q5⟧ [al-Baqarah:163]. And He said (glorified be He): ⟦Q6⟧ [al-Isra:23]. And He said (exalted be He): ⟦Q7⟧ [al-Fatihah:5]. And He said (glorified be He): ⟦Q8⟧ [al-Bayyinah:5]. And He said (mighty and majestic be He): ⟦Q9⟧ [al-Hajj:62].
Along with this fundamental, it is necessary to believe in the messengers (peace and blessings be upon them) from the time of Adam (peace and blessings be upon him) onwards. In the time of Adam, his progeny were required to follow what Allah revealed to him and legislated for him of knowledge and action, the foundation of which is the oneness of Allah, sincerity to Him, and belief in His messenger and prophet Adam (peace and blessings be upon him). In the time of Noah and after, his people were required to believe in Noah and follow what he brought, along with the oneness of Allah and sincerity to Him.
Noah (peace be upon him) was the first messenger to the people of the earth after shirk (polytheism) occurred among them. Before that, people were upon the monotheism with which Allah sent Adam (peace and blessings be upon him) and which he taught his progeny. The people of Hud were required to believe in Hud and follow what he brought, along with the oneness of Allah (glorified be He). In the time of Salih, his people were required to believe in Salih and follow what he brought, along with the oneness of Allah. Likewise, in the time of every messenger, it is necessary to affirm the oneness of Allah and belief that there is no god but Allah, and along with that, belief in the messenger and following what he brought, up to the time of Jesus (peace and blessings be upon him), the last of the prophets of the Children of Israel, Jesus son of Mary (peace and blessings be upon him). Then Allah sent their seal and the best of them, our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Jesus is the last of the prophets of the Children of Israel, and Muhammad is the last of the prophets and the seal of all messengers; there is no prophet or messenger after him (peace and blessings be upon him). He is the best of the messengers, their imam, and their seal. It is necessary for the ummah (community) of Muhammad ﷺ—jinn and humans, Arabs and non-Arabs, males and females, rich and poor, rulers and ruled—to believe in this Prophet and in the prophets and messengers before him (peace and blessings be upon them). Whoever does not believe in him has no Islam and no religion. It is necessary to believe that Allah is the true God and that there is no true god except Allah, and to believe in Muhammad ﷺ and that he is truly the Messenger of Allah to all people. Whoever does not believe in these two testimonies is not a Muslim. It is necessary to believe in them and to hold their meaning in one's heart: the meaning of "la ilaha illa Allah" is that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah. It is not permissible to worship anyone besides Allah—no angel, prophet, tree, stone, jinn, idol, or anything else. If someone says, "O Messenger of Allah, help me" after his death ﷺ, or says, "O my master al-Badawi, help me or cure my sick," or "O my master al-Husayn," or "O my master 'Abd al-Qadir," or "Help, help," or the like, this is all shirk (polytheism) with Allah (mighty and majestic be He), which nullifies the meaning of "la ilaha illa Allah." It nullifies your saying "la ilaha illa Allah," because you have not devoted worship to Allah alone; rather, you have associated others with Allah and called upon others besides Him. Allah says: ⟦Q10⟧ [al-Jinn:18]. And He says (glorified be He): ⟦Q11⟧ [Yunus:106]. And He says (glorified be He): ⟦Q12⟧ [al-Bayyinah:5]. And He says (glorified be He): ⟦Q13⟧ [al-Isra:23]. And He says (glorified be He): ⟦Q14⟧ [al-Fatihah:5]. And the Prophet ﷺ said: "Supplication is worship." And He (mighty and majestic be He) says: ⟦Q15⟧ [Ghafir:60]. So it is necessary to make worship purely for Allah alone, and among worship is supplication. If you say to a dead person, a tree, or an idol, "Help me," "Support me," "Cure my sick," etc., then that is major shirk with Allah (mighty and majestic be He), which invalidates the saying of "la ilaha illa Allah." Likewise, whoever disbelieves in Muhammad ﷺ or any of the messengers and prophets (peace and blessings be upon them), or doubts his message, or says that he was sent only to Arabs and not to non-Arabs, or says that he is not the seal of the prophets but rather a prophet will come after him—all of this is major disbelief, misguidance, and a nullification of Islam. We ask Allah for safety. From this is known the disbelief of the Qadianis for their belief in the prophethood of Mirza Ghulam Ahmad, who came many centuries after Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. It is necessary to believe that Muhammad ﷺ is truly the Messenger of Allah to all the two weighty kinds (jinn and humans), and to believe that he is the seal of the prophets and messengers; there is no prophet or messenger after him. Whoever claims prophethood after him, like Musaylimah the Liar, is a disbeliever in Allah and a liar. Likewise, al-Aswad al-'Ansi in Yemen, Sajah al-Tamimiyyah, al-Mukhtar ibn Abi 'Ubayd al-Thaqafi, and others who claimed prophethood after him (peace and blessings be upon him). The companions (may Allah be pleased with them and make them pleased) unanimously agreed on their disbelief and fought them because they denied the meaning of His saying (glorified be He): ⟦Q16⟧ [al-Ahzab:40]. And the hadiths are mutawatir (mass-narrated) from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "I am the seal of the prophets; there is no prophet after me" (peace and blessings be upon him).
So this testimony, which is the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, is the essential root and the first pillar of Islam. There is no Islam except with these two testimonies in word, deed, and belief. If a person prays, gives zakah, fasts, performs pilgrimage, and remembers Allah often, but does not believe that Allah alone is worthy of worship, then he is a disbeliever like the hypocrites. Likewise, whoever says that there is no harm in worshipping idols and images, that there is no harm in worshipping al-Badawi, al-Husayn, Sheikh 'Abd al-Qadir, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, or others among prophets, saints, angels, or jinn, whoever believes that it is permissible to worship them alongside Allah and that it is permissible to seek their help and make vows to them—he becomes a polytheist with Allah (mighty and majestic be He), and this speech and belief of his nullifies and invalidates the saying of "la ilaha illa Allah," according to the saying of Allah (glorified be He): ⟦Q17⟧ [al-An'am:88] and His saying (mighty and majestic be He): ⟦Q18⟧ [al-Zumar:65]. Likewise, if someone says that Muhammad ﷺ is not the seal of the prophets, or that he was not sent to the two weighty kinds but only to Arabs, then he is a disbeliever in Allah (mighty and majestic be He) by the text and the consensus of the people of knowledge. It is necessary for the accountable person to believe that he is the Messenger of Allah to all the two weighty kinds, and to believe that he is the seal of the prophets; there is no prophet or messenger after him. This is the essential root. Then after this, the Muslim is required to pray, give zakah, fast, perform pilgrimage, and carry out the rest of the commands and avoid the prohibitions. Along with belief that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, it is also necessary to believe in all the previous prophets, that they conveyed the message and delivered it (peace and blessings be upon them). It is also necessary, with all this, to believe in what Allah and His Messenger ﷺ have informed of what has happened and what will happen in the end times and on the Day of Resurrection⟦N19⟧.
From the program "Nur 'ala al-Darb," tape no. 16, (Majmu' Fatawa wa Maqalat al-Shaykh Ibn Baz 7/32).
